The 1960s sexual revolution is described by some sources as expanding women’s bodily autonomy and catalyzing feminist gains, including legal rights and new social freedoms [d1][d2][d5][d6]. Conversely, other evidence portrays the era as failing to liberate women, with persistent gender-based violence, objectification, and exploitative arrangements continuing or even intensifying [d3][d4][d7][d10][d11]. Scholars and critics also argue that sexual liberation has produced new harms for women and disproportionately benefited high-status men [d8][d9].
